question.text: Under Schedule VI of the SEBI (Merchant Bankers) Regulations as summarised at p.124 of the NISM-Series-IX workbook, for how long must lead managers maintain due diligence records relating to an issue (i.e., the minimum retention period explicitly stated in that paragraph)?

answer.text: 3 years from the date of listing
7 years from the date of issue closure
10 years from the date of allotment

explanation.text: The Logic: The paragraph on p.124 of the NISM-Series-IX workbook (summarising Schedule VI of the SEBI Merchant Bankers Regulations) states that lead managers must maintain due-diligence records for a minimum period of 5 years. Anchored to that specific paragraph, the unique answer is "Minimum 5 years". The Trap: 3 years aligns with other generic SEBI record-keeping windows but is not the figure used by Schedule VI. 7 years and 10 years are common distractors but neither appears as the Schedule VI minimum for lead-manager DD records. The audit flagged that elsewhere in the same workbook (p.89), pre-issue and post-issue merchant-banker records must be kept for 8 years — so anchoring the stem to a specific paragraph is necessary to make a single option uniquely correct. Note: The original stem was ambiguous because the workbook itself carries two retention periods — 5 years on p.124 for lead-manager DD records under Schedule VI, and 8 years on p.89 for the broader merchant-banker pre/post-issue records. Since no listed option gives 8 years, the stem has been tightened to anchor explicitly to the p.124 Schedule VI paragraph so that 5 years is the uniquely defensible answer.
